headline: Malaysia is studying a copyright change that would let creators stop AI companies from using their work for training.
score_reason: New, official remarks, but an early-stage study.
importance_line: Malaysian writers, artists and musicians might gain a way to keep their work out of AI training, but nothing is drafted and the official stresses the law must not stifle investment.
summary: SAYS, citing The Edge Malaysia, reports that Yusnieza Syarmila Yusoff, director-general of the Intellectual Property Corporation of Malaysia (MyIPO), said on 6 Oct 2026 that the government is exploring data-mining rules that let rights holders opt out, meaning refuse the use of their works. She said the law must not be so restrictive that it stifles trade and investment, and the review is still under discussion with stakeholders, so this is a study and not yet a proposal in law.
